chunks: From him, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn al-Fudayl, from Hamza ibn Humran, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Humran, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'The oath that necessitates expiation upon me.' So they both said: 'Whatever you swore upon, from what is obedience to Allah therein, if you were to do it but did not do it, then upon you is the expiation regarding it; and whatever you swore upon, from what is disobedience to Allah therein, then its expiation is leaving it; and whatever does not contain disobedience nor obedience, then it is nothing.'
ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for breaking an oath to do a good deed versus a bad deed in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This foundational hadith from al-Kafi, narrated by Hamzah ibn Humran, establishes the tripartite classification of oaths (al-yamin al-mu'akkadah) within Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between oaths of obedience, sin, and neutrality. It clarifies that the expiation (kaffarah) is triggered by the failure to fulfill an oath of obedience, while an oath of sin is expiated by performing the act itself, reflecting the principle that the 'sin' is the omission of the act. This ruling is central to the Shia understanding of vow fulfillment and is often cited in discussions regarding the validity of conditional oaths in daily life.

en.hubeali: From him, from Sa’ad Bin Sa’ad, from Muhammad Bin Al Qasim Bin Al Fazl, from Hamza Bin Humran, from Dawood Bin Farqad, from Humran who said,

‘I said to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The oath which necessitates the expiation upon me’. So they both said: ‘Whatever you have sworn upon (if it is) from what is obedience for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> therein if you were to do it, so you do not do it, then upon you is the expiation with regards to it; and whatever you swear upon (if it is) from what is the disobedience for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> therein, so its expiation is that you leave it; and whatever does not happen to have in it a disobedience, nor an obedience, so it is not with anything’.
en.sarwar: 3. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Sa‘d ibn Sa‘d from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn al-Fudayl from Hamzah ibn Humran from Dawud ibn Farqad from Humran who has narrated the following: “

I once asked abu Ja‘far, and abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, about the kind of oath for which I owe expiation. They said, ‘It is when you take an oath for an act in which there is obedience to Allah if you do it and you do not do it, then there is expiation on you. If you take an oath for an act in which there is disobedience to Allah then its expiation is not to do it. An oath about the act which is not an obedience or disobedience does not have any valid effect.’”
